newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan economy to contract one percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan economy to contract one percent in 1996.

text.p: The overall Venezuelan economy will contract by about one percent in 1996, a less sharp contraction than had been expected, Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said Wednesday.
"The behavior of gross domestic product (in 1996) will be minus one percent, much better than expected," Matos said during a breakfast meeting with foreign journalists.
The Venezuelan economy grew by 2.2 percent in 1995. Government officials have said it will grow by more than four percent in 1997.
Matos added that economic recovery would then pick up speed, with the GDP growing at a rate of over six percent per year from 1998 onwards.
"This implies that private investment must grow at a rate of 10 percent of GDP per year compared with two percent at present," he said.
